summary: The Federal Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act of 2026 prohibits federal agencies, including military departments, from providing federal contracts, grants, loans, or other financial assistance to individuals convicted of specific fraud-related federal felonies for a three-year period following their conviction. This prohibition also extends to any business entity where such a convicted individual is a beneficial owner. The Department of Justice must notify the General Services Administration so that these individuals can be added to the government's exclusion list. Agency heads may grant case-by-case waivers but must notify Congress in writing with a justification.

affected_groups.effect: Banned from receiving federal contracts, grants, loans, or other financial assistance for three years following conviction.
affected_groups.group: Individuals convicted of specified federal felonies

affected_groups.effect: Ineligible for federal financial assistance or contracts for three years if a beneficial owner with substantial control or 25 percent ownership is convicted of a covered felony.
affected_groups.group: Business entities with convicted beneficial owners

affected_groups.effect: Required to check exclusion lists, withhold financial assistance from barred individuals and entities, and notify Congress if they grant a waiver.

key_provisions: Prohibits federal agencies and military departments from entering into, renewing, or extending contracts or providing financial assistance to individuals convicted of covered fraud-related felonies for three years.
Extends the ban to any entity where the convicted individual is a beneficial owner, defined as exercising substantial control or owning at least 25 percent of the ownership interests.

Requires the Attorney General to timely notify the Administrator of General Services of such convictions, and requires the Administrator to promptly update the System for Award Management Exclusions list.
Allows agency heads to issue case-by-case waivers to the prohibition, provided they immediately submit a written justification to Congress.
Directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue implementation guidance within one year of enactment, and requires revisions to the Federal Acquisition Regulation.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Federal Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act of 2026 prohibits federal agencies, including military departments, from providing federal contracts, grants, loans, or other financial assistance to individuals convicted of specific fraud-related federal felonies for a three-year period following their conviction. This prohibition also extends to any business entity where such a convicted individual is a beneficial owner. The Department of Justice must notify the General Services Administration so that these individuals can be added to the government's exclusion list. Agency heads may grant case-by-case waivers but must notify Congress in writing with a justification.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a government-wide statutory ban on awarding federal funds to individuals and associated entities convicted of federal fraud-related crimes linked to government financial assistance. It standardizes exclusion procedures across all executive and military departments and introduces explicit congressional oversight for any granted waivers.

title: Federal Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act of 2026
